ov: Five living species of huge, thick-skinned plant-eaters, two in Africa and three in South and Southeast Asia. All weigh over half a tonne, and most are endangered because poachers kill them for their horns.
rg: Africa (black and white rhinos) and South and Southeast Asia (Indian, Javan and Sumatran rhinos).
df: Plants. The white rhino grazes on grass, the black rhino browses leafy shrubs, and the Sumatran and Javan rhinos do both.
fx: The two African species have no front teeth. They pluck their food with their lips.
